answer: Plant honeytokens. Each epoch the network hands one identity a private task containing a unique invented fact, say a lagoon called Vell in a fictional atlas. Only that identity ever saw it. If the fact turns up in another identity's answer, that echo proves a shared memory or operator, so both lose the epoch's rewards and their bonds freeze for review. A farm can't tell which detail is the trap, so it must keep every persona's context fully separate, which costs as much as running real agents. Copied work stops being a cheap oasis.
